Every city was conquered by the sword except the city of the Messenger, which was conquered by the Qurʾan alone; its people came to be called al-Anṣār, and you would not know an Awsī from a Khazrajī. There was a Jew living near them who had known their Jāhiliyya, their enmity and their warfare, and he hated the Muslims and envied them and attacked them a great deal. When he passed by a company of the Anṣār sitting together, brothers who loved one another, that angered him. So he went to a youth of his and said to him: I passed by a company of the Khazraj and a company of the Aws who are brothers loving one another. I would have you stand before them and say: Remember the Day of Buʿāth — that is a day of war that took place between them — on that day so-and-so and so-and-so of the Aws were killed, and so-and-so and so-and-so of the Khazraj were killed. And he recited the poems they used to recite to one another when they fought, until two men of them quarrelled, an Awsī and a Khazrajī, and they said: If that day were to return, we would do to you as we did in the past. And they said: We return to it now. So they called one another to arms. The Khazraj cried: To the Khazraj! and the Aws cried: To the Aws! They took up arms and meant to fight one another. The Messenger ﷺ went out to them with the Muhājirūn and said to them: ⟨With the cry of the Jāhiliyya, and I am here among you? Allah! Allah!⟩ So they threw down their swords and every one of them embraced his brother — and this was from al-shayṭān (Satan) — and they returned better than they had been before. And this verse was sent down concerning them[28]; it takes in brothers in Allah until the end of time. «O you who believe, if you obey a party of those who have been given the Book» — the Jews — «they will turn you back, after your faith, into unbelievers. And how can you disbelieve» (Q. 3:100–101) — a rebuke

«while the verses of Allah are recited to you and His Messenger is among you? And whoever holds fast» — clings — «to Allah, he has been guided»

«to a straight path» (Q. 3:101). «O you who believe, fear Allah as He ought to be feared» — that He be obeyed and not disobeyed, that He be thanked and not denied, that He be remembered and not forgotten[29]. They said: O Messenger of Allah, who has the strength for this? So it was abrogated by His words, Exalted:

«So fear Allah as much as you are able» (Q. 64:16). It has been said that there is no abrogation here[30]; rather, whoever fears Allah as much as he is able has feared Allah as He ought to be feared. «And do not die except as Muslims» (Q. 3:102) — affirmers of the divine oneness. «And hold fast» — cling — «to the rope of Allah» — His religion —

«all together» — the rope of Allah is the community — «and do not become divided» — do not split apart after Islam — «and remember the favour of Allah»

His bestowal of favour — «upon you» — O company of the Aws and the Khazraj — «when you were» — before Islam — «enemies, and He brought together»

joined — «your hearts» — through Islam — «so that you became» — you came to be — «by His favour brothers» — in religion and in walāya

«And you were on the brink of a pit» — on the edge of a pit — «of the Fire» — nothing stood between you and falling into it but that you should die as unbelievers — «and He saved you from it» — by faith (īmān) — «thus» — as He makes clear to you what has been mentioned — «does Allah make His verses clear to you, that you may be guided» (Q. 3:103). al-Ḥaqq has directed us in this verse to this, that the way of our success is the godfearing (al-taqwā) of Allah, Blessed and Exalted. Godfearing is of degrees. The godfearing of the generality is faith — the opposite of unbelief — faith in Allah

and compliance with the command and avoidance of the prohibition. The godfearing of the elect is that he remember Allah and not forget Him, that he thank Him and not deny Him, that he obey Him and not disobey Him. The godfearing of the elect of the elect is that nothing other than Allah ever cross the servant’s mind. To this the poet Ibn al-Fāriḍ points in his words:

⟨And were a desire for any other than You to pass over my mind, through inadvertence, I would judge myself to have apostatised.⟩[31]

That is the utmost of godfearing, that a man not turn his regard to anything other than Allah, Blessed and Exalted; and that cannot come about without the remembrance of Allah, Blessed and Exalted, with the tongue. The remembrance of Allah with the tongue is the lowest remembrance, but remembrance with the tongue is indispensable, so that he may come to remember with the heart; and remembrance with the heart is reflection. When the servant reflects, either he reflects upon his nafs, and sees the baseness of his nafs and the ugliness of its work, and then he must flee from it to Allah, Blessed and Exalted; or he reflects upon Allah and upon what is with Him, and then he must desire Him, and so he flees from the nafs and goes to Allah, Blessed and Exalted. In either case the flight is to Allah, Blessed and Exalted. And when he has fled to Allah, Blessed and Exalted, and held fast to the religion of Muhammad ﷺ, and taken on the ādāb (the proprieties) of the awliyāʾ of Allah, Blessed and Exalted, and kept their company, he must arrive at what is sought. «And hold fast to the rope of Allah, all together» (Q. 3:103) — that is, the rope of Allah is the community. ⟨The hand of Allah is with the community⟩

So whoever parts from the community is quit of the religion.[32] ⟨The hand of Allah is with the community.⟩[33] The Messenger ﷺ said: ⟨Hold to the community, for al-shayṭān flees from the community; he is nearer to two than he is to three, and nearer to one than to two.⟩[34] This division is only division in doctrines, and enmity and hatred. As for division in the branches [of the law], without mutual hostility, it does not fall under this; and to it the hadith ⟨The disagreement of my community is a mercy⟩[35] points. The Companions disagreed among themselves most severely in the branches, yet there was no enmity between them, and this is praiseworthy. As for division in doctrines, that is what brings about enmity. The Messenger ﷺ drew a straight line and drew lines around it, and said: ⟨This is my path, straight, to which I call, and these are the ways that Allah has forbidden you.⟩ «And do not follow the ways, lest they part you from»

«His path» (Q. 6:153).[36] And he ﷺ said: ⟨The Jews split into seventy-one sects, all of them in the Fire; the Christians split into seventy-two sects, all of them in the Fire; and my community will split into seventy-three sects, all of them in the Fire save one. They said: And which is that one? He said: That which I am upon, and my Companions.⟩

That is, the sunna and the community.[37]

Allah, Blessed and Exalted, reminded the believers; He reminded them — that is, He admonished them — of several things: «Hold fast to the rope of Allah» (Q. 3:103) — a command to hold fast to the Book, the sunna and the community, and not to divide; and that we should remember the favours of Allah, Blessed and Exalted, His bestowal of favour upon us. All these things require flight to Allah, Blessed and Exalted.

«And let there be among you a community calling to the good» — and let there be among you a group calling people to the good — «and enjoining what is right and forbidding what is wrong. And those» — the callers, the enjoiners, the forbidders — «they are the ones who prosper» (Q. 3:104) — they are the triumphant. The Messenger ﷺ said: ⟨Allah has servants who are neither prophets nor martyrs, whom the prophets and the martyrs envy for their nearness to Allah, Blessed and Exalted. They said: And who are they, O Messenger of Allah? He said: They are those who make people beloved to Allah and who make Allah beloved to people. They said: That they make Allah beloved to people we have understood; but how do they make people beloved to Allah? He said: They enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong, and when the people comply with the command of Allah and avoid His prohibitions, Allah loves them.⟩[38] This is a collective obligation. The Muslim community is obliged to have among it a party who call people to Allah, who enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong. He introduced min (from) to signify a part, because enjoining what is right and forbidding what is wrong is not obligatory upon all people. Conditions are required for it. Knowledge is required first: one who does not know, when he enjoins or forbids, may well forbid what is right and enjoin what is wrong. This is the cause of innovation. And he must have standing, so that his word is accepted. But if, when he forbids a wrong, he commits something worse than it, then neither enjoining what is right nor forbidding what is wrong is obligatory upon him; and when the conditions are met in him, he is obliged to enjoin what is right and to forbid what is wrong. «And those, they are the ones who prosper» (Q. 3:104). The Companions of the Messenger ﷺ used to enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong, and this is as it were the greater jihad. The Messenger said: ⟨A time will come when nothing of Islam remains but its name, and nothing of the Qurʾan but its written form. The worst of those whom the sky shades on that day will be their scholars and their reciters: their scholars through greed, and their reciters through ostentation in worship (riyāʾ).⟩ He said: ⟨You are in a time in which⟩

⟨the hearts are flourishing, and a time will come in which the hearts will be in ruins and the mosques flourishing with bodies.⟩[39] The kings grow arrogant, the rich grow miserly, the scholars grow greedy, the devotees make a show of their worship, and the merchants deal in usury. And the Messenger ﷺ said: ⟨The first to be called to account on the Day of Resurrection are three; they are brought forward: one who bore the Book of Allah, Blessed and Exalted, one who spent, and one who fought in the way of Allah and was martyred. He says to the reciter: You bore My Book — what did you do for Me? He says: I used to recite it in the watches of the night and at the ends of the day. He says: You did not intend Me by that; you intended that it be said, So-and-so is a reciter — only that; and it has been said. That is your recompense; you have nothing with Me. And He says to the rich man: What did you do for Me? I provided you with much wealth. He says: I used to give right and left, giving alms for Your sake. He said:⟩

⟨No, you did not intend Me by that; rather you wanted it to be said, ‘So-and-so is generous’ — and it has been said. Then the fighter in jihad is brought, and He says to him:⟩

⟨What did you do for Me? He says: I took up my sword and struck right and left until I was killed as a martyr. He says: You did not intend My face by that; you intended that it be said, ‘So-and-so is a hero, so-and-so is brave’ — and it has been said. These are the first for whom the Fire will be stoked.⟩[40] There must be sincerity (ikhlāṣ) of action for Allah, Blessed and Exalted, and there must be the company of the righteous

«And do not be like those who became divided» — away from their religion — «and differed» — concerning it — «after the clear proofs had come to them»

and they are the Jews and the Christians. «And those — for them is a great punishment» (Q. 3:105). Recall «the day when faces will turn white and faces will turn black» — that is, the Day of Resurrection. As for the believers, the whiteness of their faith in their hearts passes over to their faces, so that they are all of them white of face; and as for the unbelievers, the blackness of their creed passes over to their faces, so that they are black. «As for those whose faces have turned black» — and they are the unbelievers, so they are cast into the Fire, and it is said to them in rebuke — «Did you disbelieve after your faith?» — on the day the covenant was taken, when every one of you said, ‘Yes indeed’ — «so taste the punishment for what you used to disbelieve. And as for those whose faces have turned white» — and they are the believers; may Allah make us and you among them — «they are in the mercy of Allah» — in His Garden — «they abide therein forever. These» — these verses — «are the verses of Allah, We recite them to you» — O Muhammad — «in truth, and Allah does not want injustice for the worlds» — by seizing them for no crime — «and to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is in the earth» — in possession, in creation, and as servants — «and to Allah all matters are returned» (Q. 3:106–109). All matters come to pass to Allah, Blessed and Exalted. «You were»

O community of Muhammad ﷺ — in the knowledge of Allah, Exalted — «the best community brought forth» — made manifest — «for mankind» — the community of Muhammad is the best community brought forth for mankind. For what reason? «you enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong and believe in Allah» (Q. 3:110). By these qualities they attained this excellence, and so they loved Allah, and they made the people beloved to Allah, and they made Allah beloved to the people. And the community of Muhammad ﷺ is everyone who follows him, from whatever stock he has arisen — even the Jews: if they enter Islam they enter into this excellence. ʿAbdallāh b. Salām was among the righteous of the Companions,

and he was originally of the Jews. So this excellence is not a matter of Arab descent alone, as the Arabs suppose, but rather it lies with the three qualities: «you enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong and believe in Allah». The proof is that Abū Ṭālib, the brother of ʿAbdallāh the father of the Messenger ﷺ, is not of this community and did not enter into this excellence; and Salmān — we read this yesterday — ⟨Salmān is one of us, the Family of the House⟩[41]. So this excellence is attained only by following him. May Allah grant us and you to follow him ﷺ. «And if the People of the Book believed, it would be» — faith would be — «better for them» — even the People of the Book, the Jews, who are the worst of the creation of Allah, Blessed and Exalted: if they believed in Allah it would be better for them, because they would enter into this excellence which belongs to the community of Muhammad ﷺ — «Among them are the believers» — such as ʿAbdallāh b. Salām, may Allah be pleased with him, and his companions — «but most of them are the transgressors» (Q. 3:110) — the unbelievers. «They will not harm you» — that is, the Jews, O company of Muslims, in anything — «except for some hurt» — with the tongue, by reviling and by threatening — «and if they fight you they will turn their backs to you» — routed — «then they will not be helped» (Q. 3:111) — against you; rather the victory is yours over them. «Abasement has been stamped upon them wherever they are found» — wherever they are come upon, so that they have no might and no refuge — «except» — being — «by a rope from Allah and a rope from the people» — you will not find a Jew but that he is seeking the protection of one state or another; as for independence, they will never find independence; and along with that, you see no rich man among them but you take him for a poor man, from the extremity of abasement and destitution — «and they have incurred» — they returned — «wrath from Allah, and destitution has been stamped upon them. That is because they» — by reason of their having — «used to disbelieve in the verses of Allah and to kill the prophets without right. That» — is for emphasis — «is for their having disobeyed» — the command of Allah — «and they used to transgress» (Q. 3:112) — passing beyond the lawful into the forbidden. «They are not all alike» — the People of the Book are not mustawin (level) — «among the People of the Book is an upright community» — an upright group, standing firm upon the truth, such as ʿAbdallāh b. Salām — «who recite the verses of Allah in the watches of the night» — in its hours — «and they prostrate» (Q. 3:113) — they pray. «They believe»

«in Allah and the Last Day, and they enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong and hasten to good works, and those are among the righteous» (Q. 3:114). They enjoin what is right and they forbid what is wrong, and they hasten — they press forward — in good works. Hastening to good works, and pressing forward, and vying with one another: to all of these the Qurʾan has called us. He said «Hasten» (Q. 3:133), and He said «Vie with one another» (Q. 57:21), and the Messenger ﷺ said: ⟨Press forward with righteous deeds before you are kept occupied⟩[42]. And He, Exalted, said «So vie with one another in good works» (Q. 2:148), which the Messenger ﷺ explained by his words: ⟨Seize five before five: your youth before your decrepitude, your health before your sickness, your leisure before your occupation, your wealth before your poverty, and your life before your death⟩[43]. A man asked one of the righteous, saying to him: What do you say about fasting on a journey? He said: Allah, Blessed and Exalted, has commanded us to press forward and to hasten, and fasting on a journey is part of this pressing forward and hastening. He said: By Allah, he gave me an answer that is not among the answers of the jurists. «they hasten to good works» — the matter requires pressing forward and it requires hastening. Time passes without cease, and your breath is in portions. Man — numbered are his

breaths and his days, and when these are spent, death must come. Every breath that has gone out has gone out of the sum of your breaths, and every moment that passes is a portion of your life; and every day, and every week, and every month, and every year is something that is always being diminished and never increased. There must be, then, an end; there must be striving. The sea is deep — a ship is needed; the road is long — provision is needed; the Watcher is all-seeing — sincerity is needed. «And whatever good you do, you will not be denied it» — you will not lose its reward; rather you will be requited for it — «and Allah is knowing of the godfearing» (Q. 3:115), and so He requites them. «Indeed those who disbelieve, there will not avail» — ward off — «them their wealth nor their children against Allah» — against His punishment — «anything» — these two were singled out for mention here because a man sometimes wards [harm] off from himself with his wealth and sometimes seeks help from his children. «And those are the companions of the Fire; they abide therein forever. The likeness of what they spend» — the unbelievers — «in this present life» — in enmity to the Prophet ﷺ, or in voluntary alms (ṣadaqa) and the like — «is like the likeness of a wind in which there is a violent blast» — intense heat or cold — «that struck the tillage of a people» — the sown field of a people — «who had wronged themselves» — by unbelief — «and destroyed it» — so they got no benefit from it; and so too his expenditures are gone, and they get no benefit from them. «And Allah did not wrong them, but they wronged themselves» (Q. 3:116–117). The condition of an accepted deed is that the doer be a believer in Allah, intending the face of Allah, Blessed and Exalted. As for the unbelievers, when they perform some act of devotion, such as acts of voluntary alms or maintaining the ties of kinship, its likeness is as He said in the verse, «like the likeness of a wind» — only that, because the condition is missing, and one who lacks the condition does not produce what is conditioned upon it. And shirk is of two kinds: al-shirk al-jalī (manifest association of partners with Allah) and al-khafī (hidden association of partners with Allah). Just as the deeds of the unbelievers are not accepted, so too with those who make a show of their worship: Allah does not turn toward their hearts. Allah has no need of what is shared with Him; the deed in which another has a share He does not accept, and the heart in which another has a share He does not enter.[44] «O you who believe, do not take as intimates» — bosom friends; they are your friends whom you let in on your secrets — «from other than yourselves» — from those who are not of you, from among the Jews

and the Christians and the hypocrites. Do not befriend the Jews, nor the Christians, nor the hypocrites, and do not acquaint them with your secrets, for they are enemies to you.[45] «They will not spare you any ruin» — they do not fall short in working corruption against you — «They have wished» — they have longed for — «what distresses you» — they love nothing but your distress, your hardship, always, and the severity of harm upon you. «There has appeared» — there has become manifest — «the hatred» — enmity toward you — «from their mouths» — whenever they speak you understand from their speech their enmity toward you — «and what their breasts conceal» — of enmity — «is greater. We have made clear to you the signs» — of their enmity — «if you would reason» (Q. 3:118) — about that — so do not take them as allies. «Here you are, loving them» — you love them, the hypocrites and the Jews, for their kinship with you and for the friendship they stir up in falsehood — «while they do not love you» — and they do not love you, because they differ from you in religion. «And they will not cease fighting you until they turn you back from your religion, if they are able» (Q. 2:217). «The Jews will never be pleased with you, nor the Christians, until you follow their creed» (Q. 2:120). This enmity has no cure, ever. «And you believe in the Book, all of it» — in all the Books — and they do not believe in your Book. «And when they meet you they say, ‘We believe,’ and when they are alone they bite their fingertips at you» — the tips of the fingers — «out of rage» — out of the intensity of their anger at what they see of your concord with one another; this is the utmost of anger — «Say: Die in your rage» — remain in it until death, for you will never see what gladdens you among the people of faith — «Indeed Allah is knowing of what is within the breasts» (Q. 3:119) — of what is in the hearts, and among it is what these men harbour. «If good touches you» — a blessing, such as a victory or spoils — «it grieves them» — that saddens them; they never wish good for you — «and if an evil befalls you» — such as a defeat or a drought — «they rejoice at it» — so do not take them as allies; this is the plainest proof of their hostility toward you — «And if you are patient» — but if you are patient — «and godfearing» — and you fear Allah — «and it will not harm you» — will not

harm you — «their scheming, in anything» — through godfearing toward Allah and through steadfast patience (ṣabr), their enmity will never harm you. «Indeed Allah encompasses what they do» (Q. 3:120). Indeed Allah is «encompassing» — knowing — «of what they do» — of all their deeds. «And» — recall — «when you went out early from your family, assigning the believers their positions for the battle» (Q. 3:121). This verse was revealed concerning the battle of Uḥud.[46] The Prophet ﷺ met the unbelievers on the day of Badr and fought them, and Allah routed them. Seventy of their chiefs were killed and seventy of their chiefs taken captive[47], and he returned to Medina. Abū Jahl, who was their leader, was killed, and ʿUtba was killed, and Shayba and al-Walīd — those who came out for single combat on the day of Badr, saying: “Single combat!” Young men of al-Anṣār came out to them, and they said: “Equals, equals — but we want our paternal cousins.” The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: ⟨Where is ʿAlī b. Abī Ṭālib b. ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib? Where is Ḥamza b. ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib? Where is ʿUbayda — or Abū ʿUbayda — b. al-Ḥārith[48] b. ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib? Go out to these men; it is only you they are calling.⟩ So they fought one another. As for ʿAlī, he killed his opponent — he was the first to kill in the path of Allah. Ḥamza killed his opponent. Abū ʿUbayda’s leg was broken, and ʿAlī and Ḥamza came and finished off his enemy and carried him to the Prophet ﷺ. These two adversaries disputed concerning their Lord, and for this reason

ʿAlī says: ⟨I am the first who will be summoned on the Day of Resurrection to the dispute.⟩[49] When they returned, Abū Sufyān swore that he would not wash himself of major ritual impurity, nor eat the flesh of camels, nor drink wine, nor oil his locks, until he had taken revenge for these men from the Prophet ﷺ. They set about gathering armies, until he came with three thousand, two thousand of whom he had hired with his own wealth.[50] The people of falsehood are able to spend upon falsehood more than the people of truth are able to, or more than most of them. They came to Mount Uḥud before the Prophet ﷺ knew of it, and when the Prophet ﷺ learned of that he gathered his Companions and consulted them. He said to them: ⟨These enemies have come out from Mecca, and here they are at Mount Uḥud. What do you advise me?⟩ ʿAbd Allāh b. Ubayy, who was a hypocrite, said: ⟨We shall not go out to them; we shall stay in our dwellings. If they remain there, they will remain in the worst of states; and if they storm in upon us in our houses, we shall fight them inside the town, with the women and the boys helping us. But it is not our custom to go out to battle.⟩ A young man of al-Anṣār came forward and said: “O Messenger of Allah, we are upon the truth and they are upon falsehood. They have come out from Mecca to Uḥud, and we are to stay in our houses waiting for them like women? This does not befit us. Rather, let us go out to them.” This was not the opinion held by the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. Then the Prophet ﷺ went into

his house, put on his coat of mail, took up his weapon and came out. ʿAbd Allāh b. Ubayy grew angry. He had three hundred of the hypocrites as his companions, who obeyed no command but his. So the Messenger ﷺ went out with a thousand less fifty[51], while the polytheists were three thousand. The Prophet ﷺ encamped in the ravine on the Saturday, the seventh of Shawwāl, in the third year of the Hijra, and he put his back and his camp toward Uḥud and drew up their ranks evenly. He stationed a force of archers and set ʿAbd Allāh b. Jubayr over them at the foot of the mountain, and said: ⟨Drive them off from us with arrows, so that they do not come upon us from behind. And do not stir, whether we are defeated or given victory.⟩ So the matter was set in order, and Allah sent down His sakīna (the indwelling peace from God) upon His Messenger. The east wind came and cast terror into the hearts of the unbelievers, and they set about killing them. On this occasion even the women came. Hind bt. ʿUtba, the wife of Abū Sufyān, came and said that if the men fled their women would divorce them, and that if the banner of Quraysh fell that day the women would have to carry it. A man of the Banū ʿAbd al-Dār carried the banner and was killed; another took it and was killed, until fifteen had been killed over the banner of Quraysh. Then the banner fell and no one took it; a woman took it up. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: ⟨Alas for Quraysh, when their banner is in the hands of women!⟩[52] So they were given victory, and the upper hand fell to the Muslims in less time than hours. When the archers who were with ʿAbd Allāh b. Jubayr saw that the fighting was finished and that victory had fallen to the Muslims, they hurried to the spoils. ʿAbd Allāh b. Jubayr said to them: ⟨Did you not hear what the Messenger ﷺ said: ‘We do not stir, whether they conquer or are conquered’?⟩ They said to him: “The matter is finished; nothing remains but the spoils alone.” They disobeyed the command of the Messenger, and Allah cast courage into the hearts of the unbelievers, so they returned and fought

the Muslims, and killed seventy-two of them[53] on the spot, and a great number of them were wounded. The Messenger ﷺ was wounded in his forehead, and they broke his front tooth ﷺ, and Ḥamza, the Lion of Allah and the Lion of His Messenger, was martyred[54]. And remember, O Muhammad, «when you set out early from your household» — from Medina; or from your household, from the house of your family: he went out from the house of ʿĀʾisha on that day — «assigning» — settling — «the believers positions» — stations in which they were to stand — «for the battle. And Allah is hearing» — of your words — «knowing» (Q. 3:121) — of your states. And that was the day of Uḥud. «When two parties among you were minded» — and they are the Banū Salama and the Banū Ḥāritha, the two wings of the army — «to fail» — that the two of them should turn coward and withdraw from the fighting — when ʿAbd Allāh b. Ubayy the hypocrite went back, he and his companions, and said: For what are we to kill ourselves and our children? And he said to Abū Jābir al-Salamī — who had said to them, I adjure you by Allah, for your Prophet and for yourselves — If we knew there would be fighting we would follow you. But Allah made the two of them stand firm and they did not turn away. They came near to fleeing as the hypocrites fled, but Allah preserved them, so that there remained only seven hundred men with the Messenger ﷺ. «And Allah was the protector of them both» — their helper against failing — «and in Allah let the believers put their trust» (Q. 3:122) — let them rely on Him and on none besides Him. It was sent down when they had been routed, as a reminder to them of Allah’s favour, when

some of the Muslims said: How does this befall us, when we are with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and upon his religion? «And Allah did indeed help you at Badr» — a place between Mecca and Medina — «while you were lowly» — through the fewness of your numbers and of your weapons — «so fear Allah, that you may be thankful» (Q. 3:123) — for His favours. «When» — an adverbial qualifier governed by ‘He helped you’ — «you said to the believers» — promising them, by way of reassurance — «Will it not suffice you that your Lord should reinforce you» — aid you — «with three thousand of the angels sent down» (Q. 3:124). «Yes indeed» — that will suffice you. And in al-Anfāl it is ‘with a thousand’, because He reinforced them with that first, then they became three thousand, then they became five thousand, as He said, Exalted: «If you are steadfast» — in meeting the enemy — «and godfearing» — of Allah, in the matter of disobeying Him — «and they come upon you» — the polytheists — «in their onrush» — their moment — «this — your Lord will reinforce you with five thousand of the angels, marked out» (Q. 3:125) — marked with signs. And they were steadfast, and Allah fulfilled His promise to them, in that the angels fought alongside them on piebald horses, wearing yellow and white turbans which they had let hang down between their shoulders[55]. When they were steadfast on the day of Badr, five thousand of the angels came down: Jibrīl, with two thousand with him; Mīkāʾīl, with a thousand with him; Isrāfīl, with a thousand with him; the Angel of Death, with a thousand with him[56]. «And Allah made it not» — the reinforcement — «except as good tidings for you» (Q. 3:126) — and this is good tidings for the Muslims

when they know that the angels are fighting alongside them, this brings them good tidings. «and so that may be set at rest» — be still — «your hearts by it» — so do not be alarmed at the multitude of the enemy and at your own fewness — «and victory comes only from Allah» — and in reality victory does not come except from Allah, Blessed and Exalted — «the Mighty, the Wise» (Q. 3:126) — not by the angels, but from Allah, Blessed and Exalted. Victory does not come except from Allah. You will not find the word ‘victory’ in the Qurʾan but that the victory is from Allah, so that the servant may know that there is no helper but Allah: «If Allah helps you, there is none that can overcome you» (Q. 3:160), «help from Allah and a near victory» (Q. 61:13), «When the help of Allah comes» (Q. 110:1). You will not find true victory except that it is with Allah: «And Allah will surely help him who helps Him» (Q. 22:40), «If you help Allah, He will help you» (Q. 47:7). There is no helper but Allah. «And victory comes only from Allah, the Mighty, the Wise» (Q. 3:126). He did that «so that He might cut off» — destroy — «a party of those who disbelieved» — by killing and by captivity — «or abase them» — humble them by defeat — «so that they turn back» — return — «disappointed» (Q. 3:127) — not having attained what they sought. And when the Messenger’s ﷺ front tooth was broken and his face was gashed on the day of Uḥud, he said: ⟨How shall a people prosper who have dyed the face of their Prophet with blood?⟩ There was sent down «You have no part in the matter»[57] — rather, the matter belongs to Allah, so be patient — «or He may relent towards them» — or Allah may relent towards them, by Islam — «or He may punish them» — and so He leaves them to die in unbelief and punishes them — «for they are wrongdoers» (Q. 3:128) — by unbelief. If Allah wills to guide them, He guides them to Islam; and if He wills to punish them, they die in unbelief, and they deserve that, because they are wrongdoers. As for the Messenger ﷺ, he has no part in the matter. And this is the utmost in

the greatness of the Messenger ﷺ: his affair is wholly the affair of Allah, Blessed and Exalted, so much so that he has no part in his own affair. «And to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is in the earth» — in possession, in creation and in servanthood — «He forgives whom He will» — him for whom He wills forgiveness — «and He punishes whom He will». Allah, Blessed and Exalted — His forgiveness has no cause. There is no cause for the forgiveness of Allah, Blessed and Exalted; He forgives whom He wills. He has forgiven unbelievers and He has forgiven the dissolute. However far the servant has gone in the evil of his condition, if Allah wills He guides him and forgives him. Forgiveness has no cause whatever, and it is withheld from none of Allah’s creation. May Allah forgive us and you, all of us. «And He punishes whom He will». «And Allah is forgiving» — to His awliyāʾ — «merciful» (Q. 3:129) — to the people of His obedience. «O you who believe, do not consume usury, doubled and multiplied» — the usury they used to deal in during the Jāhiliyya: they would add to the sum when the term fell due and defer the demand, so that it became doubled and multiplied — «and fear Allah» — by leaving it off — «that you may prosper. And fear the Fire which has been prepared for the unbelievers» (Q. 3:130–131) — lest you be punished by it. «And obey Allah and the Messenger, that you may be shown mercy. Hasten to a forgiveness from your Lord and to a garden whose breadth is the heavens and the earth» (Q. 3:132–133). Hurry to righteous deeds, hastening to Allah’s forgiveness and hastening to Allah’s Garden, whose breadth is the heavens and the earth. The heavens are seven; the expanse of a heaven is a distance of five hundred years. One heaven is joined to another until they come to seven, and one earth is joined to another until they come to fourteen. The Garden is wider than this[58]. The Messenger ﷺ said: ⟨The place where the believer’s whip hangs in the Garden is wider than this world and all that is in it, and better than this world and all that is in it.⟩[59] The heavens and the earth are the widest thing we see, and the Qurʾan brings things near to minds; it addresses minds to the measure of what they understand. Otherwise the breadth of the Garden is not to be measured by the breadth of

the heavens and the earth. It is related that when Allah created the Garden He said to it: Extend. And it extended for a thousand years. He said to it: Extend. And it extended for a thousand years. He said to it: Extend. It said: To what extent? He said: Extend to the measure of the breadth of My mercy. And the mercy of Allah, Blessed and Exalted, has no end, and so the Garden came to have no end. Everyone who dwells in the Garden — may Allah make us and you among them — dwells in its middle; as for the edge of the Garden, no one knows it, for it has no edge. That wide Garden: hasten to it by righteous deeds. «It has been prepared for the godfearing» (Q. 3:133). That Garden is for whom? For the godfearing, by performing acts of obedience and leaving off acts of disobedience. Godfearing, wherever it is mentioned in the Qurʾan, is compliance with the command and avoidance of the prohibition. «Those who spend» — in obedience to Allah — «in ease and in hardship» — He described the godfearing with qualities, among them the spending of their wealth in the way of Allah in the state of ease and the state of difficulty — «and who restrain anger» — and those who are able to carry their anger through, and restrain the anger while able to — «and who pardon people» — those who have wronged them, leaving off their punishment — «and Allah loves those who do good» (Q. 3:134) — by these deeds, that is, He rewards them. This verse too — the righteous forebears performed noble deeds upon it. Al-Ḥasan b. ʿAlī had a steed which he loved greatly, and he sent a slave boy of his to water it and wash it, intending to set out on a journey. The boy was slow, until al-Ḥasan grew impatient; then he brought the steed, having hamstrung it — he had hamstrung its legs — and he had not washed it but had smeared it with blood. When he came, al-Ḥasan said to him: What moved you to this? He said: I wished only for your anger. He said: al-shayṭān incited you to this, but I shall rub his nose in the dust. Allah, Blessed and Exalted, says in His Book «and who restrain anger», and I have restrained my anger. He said to him: But the Qurʾan added something. He said: «and who pardon people». He said: I have pardoned you. He said: «and Allah loves those who do good». He said: You are free, for the sake of Allah, and the steed is a gift from me to you. Those who restrain anger, and pardon those who have wronged them, and do good — three qualities. Out of His bounty He said: «And those who, when they have committed an indecency» — a foul sin, such as fornication — «or wronged themselves» — by something lesser than it, such as a kiss — «remember Allah» — His threat — «and so seek forgiveness for their sins — and who forgives» — they know that none forgives — «sins but Allah — and they did not persist» (Q. 3:135) — did not continue

«upon what they did» — rather, they desisted from it — «while they know» (Q. 3:135) — that what they had committed was an act of disobedience. This is the fourth category. «Those — their recompense is forgiveness from their Lord, and gardens beneath which rivers run, abiding therein» — that is, destined for everlasting abiding (khulūd) therein — «and excellent is the reward of those who work» (Q. 3:136) — in obedience. This is the reward. Whoever commits a sin and recites this verse, «And those who, when they commit an indecency or wrong themselves, remember Allah and ask forgiveness for their sins — and who forgives sins but Allah?» (Q. 3:135), and asks forgiveness of Allah, Blessed and Exalted, Allah forgives him. ⟨My servant, I shall not cease to forgive you so long as you keep asking My forgiveness. Were you to come to Me with sins enough to fill the earth and then ask My forgiveness, I would forgive you and not care.⟩[60] ⟨Had you not sinned, Allah would have taken you away and brought a people who sin and ask forgiveness, and He would forgive them.⟩[61] ⟨Had you not sinned, I would have feared for you something greater than it: self-admiration, self-admiration.⟩[62] Allah, Blessed and Exalted, does not love disobedience and does not love the disobedient, but He loves those who turn to Him in repentance; and those who turn to Him in repentance are none but the disobedient who repent (tāʾib). «There have passed away» — gone by — «before you ways» — courses taken with the unbelievers, in granting them respite and then seizing them — «So travel» — O believers — «in the land and see how the end of those who denied was» (Q. 3:137) — the messengers. The end of their affair was destruction, nothing else. So do not grieve at their gaining the upper hand, for I am granting them respite until their time. The unbelievers

and the wrongdoers are granted respite, they are not neglected. Allah grants respite, He does not neglect. You will not find a wrongdoer but that he is afflicted with another wrongdoer, and then Allah destroys them all. «And such is the seizing of your Lord when He seizes the towns while they are doing wrong. Indeed His seizing is painful, severe» (Q. 11:102). ⟨Allah grants the wrongdoer respite, or gives the wrongdoer rein, until, when He seizes him, He does not let him go.⟩[63] «This» — the Qurʾan — «is a plain exposition for the people» — all of them — «and a guidance» — from error — «and an admonition for the godfearing» (Q. 3:138) — among them. «And do not weaken» — do not grow feeble in fighting the unbelievers — «and do not grieve» — over what befell you at Uḥud — «for you are the higher» — in overcoming them — «if you are believers» (Q. 3:139) — truly. If faith is true with us, then we are the higher always. This is a promise from Allah, Blessed and Exalted, and He fulfilled it for those before us: when they were true in their faith, Allah gave them victory and set them above all. «If a wound touches you» — a gash — «the people have indeed been touched» — the unbelievers — «by a wound» — a gash — «like it» — at Badr. How is it that you are in pain, O Muslims, when what befell you befell the unbelievers? «And those days — We turn them about» — We cause them to come round — «among the people» — a day for one party and a day for another; a day against us and a day for us, that they may take heed — «and that Allah may know» — a knowing that makes manifest — «those who believe» (Q. 3:140). What is intended by this, and it is for trial, is that He may know those who are true in their faith. Had victory been always the ally of the Muslims, no trial would have fallen that distinguishes the believers from the hypocrites. «And whoever fights in the way of Allah and is killed or conquers» (Q. 4:74). He put «and is killed» first because it may be that the one who wages jihad in the way of Allah is killed. «or conquers» — then he conquers also. Had He loved only what agrees with the souls, He would have said: and whoever fights in the way of Allah and conquers. He was able to say this, but «and is killed» — it may be that he is killed before he attains what he sought, or that he conquers. «and that He may take witnesses from among you» — He honours them with martyrdom — «and Allah does not love the wrongdoers» (Q. 3:140) — the unbelievers; rather He punishes them, and what He bestows upon them of favour is istidrāj (being drawn on to ruin by degrees),

whenever the unbeliever among them finds a favourable opportunity, it is nothing but istidrāj, and its end is destruction; and as for the Muslim, whatever befalls him is nothing but trial, and its end is victory. «and so that Allah may purge those who believe» — purify them — «and destroy» — annihilate — «the unbelievers» (Q. 3:141). «Or» — rather — «did you suppose that you would enter the Garden while Allah has not yet known those of you who waged jihad» — do you suppose that submission (islām) is mere words, and that you will enter the Garden? Rather, not until Allah knows those of you who waged jihad, a knowing that makes manifest. Allah knows every thing, but the knowing here is a making manifest to the people — «and may know the steadfast» (Q. 3:142) — in hardships. «And you were indeed wishing for death before you met it» (Q. 3:143) — O Muslims. You used to wish for it when the Battle of Badr took place, and the Messenger said: ⟨Perhaps Allah looked upon the people of Badr and said: Do what you will, for I have forgiven you.⟩[64]

Every one of you wished to be present at a battle like Badr, so as to attain what the people of Badr attained. You used to wish for this, and today you fled. «Now you have seen it» — you have seen the cause of death, which is war — «while you were looking on» (Q. 3:143) — clear-sighted, pondering the state of affairs. So why were you routed? A severe rebuke to those of them who fled on the day of Uḥud.

And it was revealed concerning their rout, when it was put about that the Prophet ﷺ had been killed. Iblīs the accursed cried out and said: Muhammad has been killed! Lo, Muhammad is slain! Lo, Muhammad is slain! So it spread abroad that the Prophet ﷺ had been killed. Abū Sufyān then came and called out: O Muhammad! O Muhammad! The Messenger ﷺ said: ⟨Do not answer him.⟩ So they kept silent. O Abū Bakr! O Abū Bakr! The Messenger said: ⟨Do not answer him.⟩ O ʿUmar! O ʿUmar! The Messenger ﷺ said: ⟨Do not answer him.⟩ He said: As for these, they have all been killed. The Prophet ﷺ said: ⟨Do not answer him.⟩ Then he raised up his idol and said: Be exalted, Hubal! Be exalted, Hubal! Be exalted, Hubal! We have al-ʿUzzā and you have no ʿUzzā. The Messenger ﷺ said: ⟨Answer him now: Allah is our Protector and you have no protector; Allah is higher⟩

⟨and more majestic; Allah is higher and more majestic; Allah is higher and more majestic.⟩ ʿUmar answered him: ⟨Every one you called upon is sitting here alive, and you will see what will rub your nose in the dust.⟩[65] He knew then that ʿUmar had not been killed, and so long as ʿUmar was there the rest were present too. When Iblīs said that Muhammad had been killed, ʿAbdallāh b. Ubayy b. Salūl turned back and said: Let me take you to your brethren the unbelievers; you will make peace with them and return to your religion and to your land. I always knew that Muhammad’s affair would never be brought to completion. This is nothing. Go to your brethren.[66] Allah, Blessed and Exalted, said: «And Muhammad is only a messenger; messengers have passed away before him. If then he dies or is killed» — like the others — «will you turn back on your heels?» (Q. 3:144). Even were it true that Muhammad had been killed, he is not the Lord (rabb); he is only a messenger. If then he dies or is killed, will you go back to unbelief, as though the religion belonged to Muhammad? The religion belongs to Allah, Blessed and Exalted, and Allah is living and does not die. Muhammad was never one who is worshipped; he only called you to the worship of Allah. How then do you turn back? «And whoever turns back on his heels will not harm Allah at all» — he only harms himself — «and Allah will reward the thankful» (Q. 3:144) — thankful for His favours, by standing firm. «And it is not for any soul to die except by Allah’s permission» — no soul dies until its term has run out — «as a thing written» — Allah has written that as a writ with Him — «with its term appointed» (Q. 3:145) — set to a time, neither coming before it nor after it. So why were you routed? Rout does not ward off death, and standing firm does not cut life short. «And whoever desires the reward of this world» — his recompense from it — «We shall give him of it, and whoever desires the reward of the hereafter, We shall give him of it» — of its reward — «and We shall reward the thankful» (Q. 3:145). The name of the Messenger ﷺ is Muhammad and Aḥmad, and whoever loves Muhammad ﷺ so much that he names his son Muhammad, the intercession of the Messenger

ﷺ. ⟨al-Jalīl has sworn that He will not punish a servant whose name is Muhammad or Aḥmad.⟩[67] For this reason the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: ⟨There is no [harm] upon any one of you that there be in his house a Muhammad, and two Muhammads, and three.⟩[68] You may have a son and name him Muhammad, and another Muhammad, and another Muhammad; this does no harm. There was a man of the Children of Israel who lived eighty years and never did a single good deed, except that whenever he looked into the Torah and saw the name of Muhammad he kissed it. When he died they cast him out and refused to pray over him. Then Gabriel called the Prophet of Allah and said to him: ⟨Go out and pray over the walī of Allah, Blessed and Exalted.⟩ He said: ⟨This dissolute reprobate, a walī of Allah?⟩ He said: ⟨He never saw the name of Muhammad without kissing it.⟩[69] He is the ḥabīb (beloved) of Allah and what He desired of all that He created. «And how many a prophet was killed» — if Muhammad has been killed, many of the prophets were killed — «with him were devoted men» — a company — «many, yet they did not weaken» — they did not turn coward — «for what befell them in the path of»

«Allah» — of wounds and the slaying of their prophets — «nor did they grow weak» — in the jihad — «nor did they submit» — they did not yield to their enemy on account of the death of their prophet, as you yourselves did when it was said that the Prophet ﷺ had been killed — «and Allah loves the steadfast» (Q. 3:146) — He rewards them. «And their saying was nothing» — at the killing of their prophet, together with their holding firm and their steadfast patience — «except that they said: Our Lord, forgive us our sins and our excesses» — our going beyond bounds — «in our affair» — giving notice that what befell them was for the evil of their own doing, and in abasement of themselves — «and make our feet firm» — with strength for the jihad — «and help us against the unbelieving people» (Q. 3:147). «So Allah gave them the reward of this world» — the victory and the spoils — «and the goodly reward of the hereafter» — the Garden […] — «And Allah loves those who do good» (Q. 3:148). «O you who believe, if you obey those who disbelieve» — in what they command you

«they will turn you back on your heels» — to unbelief — «and you will turn back as losers» (Q. 3:149). «Rather, Allah is your Protector» — your helper — «and He is»

«the best of helpers» (Q. 3:150) — so obey Him and not them. «We shall cast terror into the hearts of those who disbelieve» — when, after they had set off from Uḥud, they resolved to come back and to root out the Muslims, and they were struck with terror and did not return — «for that they associated partners» — because of their associating partners — «with Allah, that for which He has sent down no authority» — no proof for its worship, and that is the idols — «and their refuge is the Fire, and evil is the abode» — the dwelling — «of the wrongdoers» (Q. 3:151) — the unbelievers; it is their dwelling. «And Allah was true to you in His promise» — to you, with the victory. Allah promised the Muslims the victory, and He was true to His promise and gave them the victory — «when you were slaying them» — killing them — «by His leave, until, when you lost heart» — you turned coward in the fighting — «and quarrelled» — you differed — «concerning the matter» — you went against the command of the Messenger ﷺ to hold the position at the foot of the mountain for the shooting. Some of you said: We will go, for our companions have been given the victory; and some of you said: We will not go against the command of the Prophet ﷺ — «and you disobeyed» — His command, and so you left the station to seek the spoils — «after He had shown you» — Allah — «what you love» — namely the victory — «Among you are some who desire this world» — and so he left the station for the spoils — «and among you are some who desire the hereafter» — and so he held firm to it until he was killed, like ʿAbdallāh b. Jubayr and his companions — «then He turned you away from them» — from the unbelievers — «that He might try you» — to put you to the test, so that the sincere might be shown apart from the rest — «and He has pardoned you» — for what you committed at Uḥud — «and Allah is possessed of bounty toward the believers» (Q. 3:152) — by the pardon. Allah, Blessed and Exalted, said that He was true to them in His promise, but that they went against the command of the Messenger ﷺ, and He said: «Among you are some who desire this world». Abū Bakr al-Ṣiddīq said: ⟨I did not think that among the Companions of the Messenger there was anyone who loved this world, before this verse.⟩ He had supposed that there was none among them who loved anything of this world, until this verse came: «Among you are some who desire this world». How astonishing! Is there among the Companions of the Messenger one who loves this world? Abū Bakr is not of them. «And among you are some who desire the hereafter». Whoever works for this world is denied the hereafter, and whoever works for the hereafter, Allah gives him what has been apportioned to him of this world and gives him the hereafter along with it. One of the Companions asked the Messenger ﷺ: ⟨How are we to know whether we are in a state pleasing to⟩

⟨Allah, or in a state that is not pleasing?⟩ He said: ⟨If, whenever you intend an act of obedience, Allah makes it easy for you, and whenever you intend an act of disobedience, Allah makes it hard for you, then you are in a good state.⟩ And remember «when you were climbing away» — going far off in the land in flight — «and not turning» — not inclining — «to anyone» — every one of you fleeing headlong, not one of you turning to look at another — «while the Messenger was calling you from your rear» — and the Prophet ﷺ behind you, saying: ⟨To me! To me, servants of Allah!⟩ — «So He requited you» — repaid you — «with grief» — by the defeat — «upon grief» — because of your grieving the Messenger ﷺ by going against him. ʿUmar was asked: Did you flee on the day of Uḥud? He said: ⟨Yes. All of us fled except the Messenger ﷺ. I saw myself running as though I were a mountain goat.⟩ On that day every one of them fled except Ṭalḥa b. ʿUbaydallāh alone; he it was who remained with the Messenger ﷺ. But ʿUmar, Abū Bakr, ʿAbd al-Raḥmān and ʿAlī soon came back to the Messenger ﷺ, and they carried him and climbed the mountain with him; and when the Companions saw him they all returned. «so that you might not grieve over what you had missed» — of the spoils — «nor over what befell you» — of the slaying — «and Allah is aware of what you do» (Q. 3:153). «Then He sent down upon you, after the grief, a security» — Allah sent down safety — «a drowsiness overcoming a party of you» — when the Companions had come back and faced the unbelievers, Allah sent down safety upon them, so that every one of them was dozing in the place of battle; and when the unbelievers saw this they said: These are not human beings — who dozes in such a place? — and so they simply fled — «while a party whose own souls had engrossed them» — their souls carried them off into anxiety, so that they had no desire but their own deliverance — «thinking of Allah» — a thought — «otherwise than the truth, the thought of the Jāhiliyya» — like the thought of the Jāhiliyya, in that they believed the Prophet had been killed — «saying: Have we» — we have nothing — «any part in the matter?» «Say: the matter belongs wholly to Allah» — the decree is His; He does what He wills — «they hide within themselves what they do not disclose» — show — «to you. They say: Had we had any part in the matter, we would not have been killed»

«here» — had the choice been ours we would not have gone out, and so we would not have been killed; but we were brought out unwillingly — «Say: Had you been in your houses»

and among you were those for whom Allah had decreed the slaying — «there would surely have gone forth» — come out — «those for whom the slaying was decreed, to their resting places»

their places of slaughter, and so they are killed. «And so that Allah might try» — test — «what is in your breasts» — your hearts — of sincerity

and hypocrisy. «And so that He might purge» — distinguish — «what is in your hearts; and Allah is knowing of what lies in the breasts» (Q. 3:154) — of what is in the hearts — nothing is hidden from Him. He tries them only so that it may appear to people. «Indeed those of you who turned away» — from the fighting — «on the day the two hosts met» — the host of the Muslims and the host of the unbelievers, at Uḥud; and they were the Muslims, all but twelve men — «it was only that Satan made them slip» — made them stumble — by his whispering — «by some of what they had earned» — of sins. This verse shows that a man commits a minor sin and the minor sin carries him on to committing a grave one. Every sin a Muslim commits is on account of a sin before it. «And Allah has indeed pardoned them. Indeed Allah is forgiving» — to the believers — «forbearing» (Q. 3:155). «O you who believe, do not be like those who disbelieved» — the hypocrites — «and said to their brothers» — that is, concerning them — «when they travelled» — journeyed — «in the land» — and died — «or were on a raid» — the plural of ghāzī, and so they were killed — «‘Had they been with us they would not have died and would not have been killed’» — do not say as they say — «so that Allah may make that» — that saying, in the outcome of their affair — «a regret in their hearts. And Allah gives life and gives death» — sitting back does not ward off death — «and Allah is seeing of what you do» (Q. 3:156), and so He requites you for it. «And if you are killed in the path of Allah» — jihad — «or die» — on your beds — «then forgiveness» — coming — «from Allah» — for your sins — «and mercy» — which is the Garden — «are better than what you amass» (Q. 3:157) — of this world and what is in it. «And if you die or are killed, to Allah you will be gathered» (Q. 3:158). If you die or are killed, the gathering is to Allah, Blessed and Exalted. The servants fall into classes: one who worships Allah out of fear of His Fire, one who worships Allah out of desire for His Garden, and one who worships Allah out of love for Him; and the verse points to all of them: «And if you are killed in the path of Allah or die, then forgiveness from Allah» — those who worship Allah out of fear of the Fire, theirs is the forgiveness; and those who worship Allah out of desire for the Garden, «and mercy are better» for them «than what you amass» — they have found the Garden, which is the mercy of Allah, Blessed and Exalted; and those who worship Allah out of love for Him, «to Allah you will be gathered». «So it was by a mercy from Allah that you were gentle» — O Muhammad — «to them» — your character was made easy toward the Muslims, by a mercy from Allah — He made the Prophet ﷺ mild and gentle. «And had you been harsh» — ill-natured — «hard of heart» — rough, and had dealt harshly with them — «they would have scattered» — they would have dispersed — «from around you. So pardon» — overlook

«them, and ask forgiveness for them» — for their sins — «and consult them» — draw out their opinions — «in the matter» — in your affair, concerning war, or to set their hearts at ease, and so that your practice might be followed after you. He ﷺ consulted them often — «And when you have resolved» — upon carrying through what you intend, after consultation — «then rely upon Allah» — trust in Him — «Indeed Allah loves those who rely» (Q. 3:159) — upon Him. «If Allah helps you» — aids you against your enemy — «then none can overcome you; and if He forsakes you, then who is there to help you» — no one will help you — «after Him? And upon Allah let the believers rely» (Q. 3:160) — not upon any other. Reliance (tawakkul) is the servant’s trust in Allah, Blessed and Exalted, even while he enters into the means. The Messenger ﷺ mentioned: ⟨Allah has given me seventy thousand of my community who will enter the Garden with no reckoning and no punishment. They said: Who are they, O Messenger of Allah? He said: They are those who do not perform incantations and do not seek incantations, and who rely upon Allah.⟩[70] ʿUmar said to him: ⟨Ask your Lord to increase you.⟩ He said: ⟨I asked Him, and He gave me, with every one of the seventy thousand, seventy thousand more.⟩ He said: ⟨Ask your Lord to increase you.⟩ He said: ⟨I asked Him, and He gave me three handfuls from the handfuls of al-Raḥmān.⟩ Someone said: ⟨Ask your Lord to increase you.⟩ ʿUmar said: ⟨Do not ask Him. Allah is able to bring us all into the Garden in a single handful; Allah scoops with His two hands three times.⟩ The Messenger ﷺ said: ⟨ʿUmar has spoken truly.⟩ ⟨They do not perform incantations and do not seek incantations⟩ means the healing incantation (ruqya) that runs against the shariʿa. Otherwise, it has been reported that the Messenger said: ⟨And what makes you know that it is an incantation?⟩[71] Fātiḥat al-Kitāb is an incantation; he named it an incantation, and had it been forbidden the Messenger

ﷺ would not have named it an incantation. When the Prophet ﷺ complained of an illness he would recite the protective suras[72] — al-Ikhlāṣ and the two suras of refuge — then breathe into his hand and wipe his head and whatever he could reach of his body, so much so that when he fell ill with the illness of his death ʿĀʾisha took to reciting the protective suras and breathing into the hands of the Messenger ﷺ, because the hands of the Messenger ﷺ are more blessed than her own hands, and to wiping, with the hands of the Messenger ﷺ, over the body of the Messenger ﷺ.[73] And he said: ⟨Whoever among you is able to benefit his brother, let him do so.⟩[74] So then the forbidden incantation, the one that runs against reliance, is the incantation by foreign names, in which there may be the names of an idol or the names of their unbelieving kings, and that is shirk; this stands apart from faith. But as for [incantation] by the Qurʾan, by the [divine] names, and by Arabic supplications (adʿiya) whose meaning is understood, that does not run against reliance. «And it is not for a prophet to defraud» — the occasion of its revelation: a red velvet cloak went missing on the day of Badr, and some of the hypocrites said that perhaps it was the Prophet ﷺ who had taken it.[75] It is not fitting for a prophet to defraud, that is, to betray a trust in the spoils; so do not suppose that of him — «and whoever defrauds will come on the Day of Resurrection with what he took» — carrying it on his neck[76] — «then every soul will be repaid» — the one who defrauded

and others — the recompense for «what it earned, and they will not be wronged» (Q. 3:161). Then it [the cloak] turned up in the possession of a man. «Is one who follows the good pleasure of Allah» — who obeyed and did not defraud — «like one who has brought upon himself» — returned with — «wrath from Allah» — for his disobedience — «and whose refuge is Hell? And evil is the destination» (Q. 3:162). «They are degrees» — possessors of degrees — «with Allah» — differing in their stations. So for the one who follows His good pleasure there is reward, and for the one who brings upon himself His wrath there is punishment. On the Day of Resurrection banners will be raised: the banner of truthfulness for Abū Bakr al-Ṣiddīq, with the veracious (ṣiddīqūn) all beneath it; and the banner of justice for ʿUmar, so that every just commander will be beneath ʿUmar’s banner; and those who spend, their banner is in the hand of ʿUthmān; and the ulama, their banner is in the hand of ʿAlī, may Allah ennoble his face; and the banner of the reciters is in the hand of Ubayy b. Kaʿb; and the banner of the call to prayer (adhān) is in the hand of Bilāl; and so likewise every people of a quality have a banner that is in the hand of their chief among the Companions[77]. These are the degrees that Allah mentioned in this verse. «And Allah is seeing of what they do» (Q. 3:163). «Allah has indeed conferred a favour upon the believers in that He sent among them a messenger from among themselves» — Allah honoured the believers when He sent among them an Arab messenger like themselves, so that they might understand from him and be ennobled through him, and not an angel and not a non-Arab — «who recites to them His verses» — the Qurʾan — «and purifies them» — cleanses them of sins — «and teaches them the Book and wisdom» — the sunna — «though they were before» — before his being sent — «in manifest error» (Q. 3:164). Before the sending of the Prophet ﷺ the Arabs were in manifest error. They had no distinction before the Messenger ﷺ and none before the Qurʾan. Their excellence, then, is by following the Qurʾan and the Messenger, and by nothing else. «Or when a misfortune struck you» — at Uḥud, with seventy of you killed — «you had already inflicted twice the like of it» — at Badr, with seventy killed and seventy taken captive — «you said» — in astonishment — «How» — from where has this come to us — «is this?» — this forsaking: how does Allah, Blessed and Exalted, forsake us when we are Muslims and the Messenger of Allah is among us? — «Say: it is from yourselves» — the forsaking came only from you; you are the ones who left the post the Prophet ﷺ had fixed for you — «Indeed Allah is powerful over everything» (Q. 3:165). Allah is powerful over everything, and among that is the giving of help and the withholding of it; and He has requited you for your contravention.

«And what struck you on the day the two hosts met» — at Uḥud — «was by the permission of Allah» — by His will — «and that He might know» — Allah, with a knowledge of outward manifestation —

«the believers» (Q. 3:166) — truly — «and that He might know those who played the hypocrite» — and those — «to whom it was said» — when they turned back from the fighting, and they were ʿAbd Allāh b. Ubayy and his companions — «Come, fight in the way of Allah» — His enemies — «or drive back» — the enemy host from us, by swelling your numbers (sawād); whoever swells the numbers of a people is one of them — if you will not fight. «They said, had we known» — were we skilled in — «fighting, we would have followed you». He, Exalted, said, giving them the lie: «They were that day nearer to unbelief than to faith» — by the abandonment of the believers which they had shown; and before that they had been nearer to faith, as to outward appearance — «they say with their mouths what is not in their hearts» — and had they been skilled in fighting they would not have followed you — «and Allah knows best what they conceal» (Q. 3:167) — of hypocrisy — «Those who said of their brothers» — in religion — «while they themselves sat back» — and they had indeed sat back from the jihad — «had they obeyed us» — that is, the martyrs of Uḥud: our brothers, had they obeyed us in sitting back — «they would not have been killed. Say: then ward off death from yourselves, if you are truthful» (Q. 3:168)

If sitting back keeps death away, then beware of death: do not die at all, ever — and yet you must inevitably die. «And do not think those who were killed» — who were martyred — «in the way of Allah to be dead; rather they are alive with their Lord» — their souls are in the crops of green birds that range through the Garden wherever they wish, as comes in the hadith[78] — «provided for» (Q. 3:169) — they eat of the fruits of the Garden — «rejoicing in what Allah has given them of His bounty, and» — they — «they receive good tidings concerning those who have not joined them, left behind them» — of their brothers — «that no fear shall be upon them, nor shall they grieve» (Q. 3:170). They asked Allah for a return to this world, so that they might give the Muslims the good news that whoever is martyred finds a full recompense of karāmāt (saintly miracles). Allah, Blessed and Exalted, said: as for the return to this world after death, there is no way to it; but I shall convey word on their behalf. So they said: convey to our brothers the Muslims that we have met our Lord, and He is pleased with us and we are pleased with Him. O Allah, bless our master Muhammad and grant him peace.
arabicBody:
أعوذ بالله من الشيطان الرجيم بسم اللّٰه الرحمن الرحيم اللهم صل على سيدنا محمد الفاتح لما أغلق والخاتم لما سبق ناصر الحق بالحق والهادي إلى صراطك المستقيم وعلى آله حق قدره ومقداره العظيم ورضي اللّٰه تعالى عن أصحاب رسول اللّٰه صلى اللّٰه عليه وسلم، ولا حول ولا قوة إلا بالله العلي العظيم
يا همة الشيخ احضري
لنا بهذا المحضر
ولتعطفي بنظرة
تأتي لنا بالظفر
(لَن تَنَالُواْ الْبِرَّ} ثوابه وهو الجنة {حَتَّى تُنفِقُواْ} تصدقوا{ مِمَّا تُحِبُّونَ) لا تجدون الجنة إلا بإنفاق بعض ما تحبون من أموالكم. ليس الإنفاق فحسب بل إنفاق ما تحب. مولانا يخاطبنا بقوله «لَى تَنَالُواْ ألْبِرَّ حَتَّىٰ تُنفِقُواْ مِمَّا تُحِبُّونٌ» بسبب نزول هذه الآية تصدق أبو طلحة بجنته بيرحاء، أرض فيها نخيل وفيها بئر أعذب ماء من مياه المدينة، كان الرسول صلى اللّٰه عليه وسلم يدخل بيرحاء ويستعذب ماء فيها. قال للرسول صلى اللّٰه عليه وسلم:
ربنا يقول «لَى تَنَالُواْ أُلْبِرَّ حَتَّىٰ تُنفِقُواْ مِمَّا تُحِبُّونٌ»، أحب أموالي إلي بيرحاء وهي في سبيل اللٰه ضعها حيث أراك الله. فقال الرسول صلى اللّه عليه وسلم: بخِ بخِ ذلك مال رابح أو مال رايح وأرى أن تضعها في الأقربين، فقسمها بين أقاربه[1]. فأتى زيد بن حارثة وقال
أحب أموالي إلي جواد عندي وهاهو جعلته في سبيل الله، فدفعه لأسامة ابنه[2] . تزول مني الآية تفاخر الصحابة ودفعوا أموالا طائلة، وكان عبد اللّٰه بن عمر يحب اللوز بالسكر وكان يشتريه دائما ويفرقه في الناس ويقول: إن عبد اللّٰه بن عمر يحب اللوز بالسكر ومولانا يقول «لَن تَنَالواْ ألْرَّ حَتَّىٰ تُنِفِقُوا مِمَّا تَحِبُّونَ». كان عمر بن عبد العزيز يهوى جارية لزوج وطلبها منها مرارا فأبت، فلما ولي الخلافة هيأتها المرأة وحلتها بأنواع الحلي والحلل ودخلت بها إليه وقالت هي هدية مني إليك تخدمك، فسألها: من أين ملكتها؟ فقالت: إنَّها جاءن بِها من بيت أبيها، ففتش كيف ملكها أبوها، فقيل مات عامل وعليه ديون فأخذ أمول فهي من تلك الأموال، فأحضر ورثة العامل فأرضاهم وتوجه إليها وقال: أنت حرة في سيل الله، أنت حرة لوجه الله. فقيل له: بعدما تعبت فيها وبرأتها من كل شبهة؟ قال: مولانا يقول «لَن تَنَالواْ أُلبرَّ حَتَّىٰ تُنفِقُواْ مِمَّا تَحِبُّونَ»[3]. وكان فُضيل مريضا فاشتهى لحم دجاج
وجاهد نفسه أربعين ليلة يزجرها عن شهوة لحم الدجاج، بعد أربعين ليلة غلبته النفس على شهوة الدجاج فأخبر ربة البيت: إني أكابد نفسي وأمنعها من شهوة لحم الدجاج وغلبتني فاليوم لابد لي من لحم الدجاج. قالت: سبحان الله، لِمَ تمنعها من شيء أحله اللّٰه وهو متيسر عليك؟ ذهبت إلى السوق واشترت دجاجا بدرهم ودانقين وطبخت الدجاج بأنواع الطباق فأحضرته بين يديه فوقف سائل وقال: تصدقوا على المسكين، فقال: ادفعيه له، فقالت: هذا شيء تحبه وأنا صنعته لك أفعل شيئا للمسكين أفضل له وتأكل شهوتك.
قال: ما تفعلين للمسكين؟ قالت: أعطيه ثمن الدجاج، ذلك أنفع له وتأكل أنت الدجاج، فقال: نِعم ما رأيت آتيني بالثمن، فأتته بالثمن، فجمع الثمن والدجاج ودفعهما للمسكين وقال: مولانا يقول «لَن تَنَالُواْ ألْبِرَّ حَتَىٰ تُنفِقُواْ مِمَّا تُحِبُّونٌ»[4]. في الحقيقة إن كان اللّٰه يخبرنا أننا لا ننال البر إلا بإنفاق بعض ما نحب فكيف ننال البَرّ؟ إلا بعد إنفاق جميع ما نملك.
البر نناله بجزء مما لَنا، والبَرُّ الذي هو اللّه لا نجده إلا بإنفاق كل ما عندنا، فلابد أن يسلم العبد أمواله وأولاده ونفسه لله تبارك وتعالى، فإذا فعل ذلك كان لله ومن كان لله كان اللّٰه له. لابد من متابعة ملة إبراهيم، إبراهيم سلّم أمواله للضيفان وولده للقربان ونفسه للنيران[5] فاتخذه اللّٰه خليلا وقال "وَمَا كَانَ مِنَ الْمُشْرِكِينُ". العبد لابد أن يتوجه إلى اللّٰه تبارك وتعالى بكليته فينال محبة اللّٰه وينال ولاية الله، لابد من محبة اللّٰه أولا ولابد من محبة أولياء الله، فمحبة أولياء اللّٰه ليست من الشرك كما يقول بعض أهل قلة الفهم، إنما هي من محبة الله. أخبر الرسول صلى اللّٰه عليه وسلم أن العبد يوقف بين يدي اللّٰه يوم القيامة فيقول له
الرب تبارك وتعالى: ماذا عملت لي؟ أما زهدك في الدنيا فاخترت الراحة لنفسك، وأما طاعتك لي فاخترت العز لنفسك، هل واليت في وليا قط أو عاديت في عدوا؟[6] إن كان والى وليا لله أو عادى عدوا لله فذلك هو العمل الذي يحببه إلى اللّٰه تبارك وتعالى، ومن حاول الوصول إلى اللّٰه تبارك وتعالى وادعى المقامات بغير محبة أولياء اللّٰه فهو كاذب ولو أتى بعبادة الثقلين فإنما يضرب حديدا باردا. لابد من موالاة أولياء اللّه ومعاداة أعداء اللّٰه فيسلك بذلك سبيل إبراهيم كما سيذكر في الآية {وَمَا تُنفِقُواْ مِن شَيءِ فَإِنَّ اللهَ بِهِ عَلَيَم} فيجازي عليه (كُلُّ الطَّعَامِ كَانَ حِلّاࣰ لِّبَنِےٓ إِسْرَاءِيلَ) نزلت لما أتى اليهود وقالوا للرسول صلى اللّٰه عليه وسلم إنك تزعم أنك على ملة إبراهيم وكان إبراهيم لا يأكل لحوم الإبل وألبانها وأنت تأكلها، فقال لهم الرسول صلى اللّٰه عليه وسلم: أنشدكم بالله هل تعلمون أن يعقوب مرض مرضا شديدا فنذر إن شفاه اللّٰه من مرضه ليتركن أحب الطعام إليه وهو لحوم الإبل وأحب الشراب إليه وهو ألبان الإبل؟ قالوا: نعم، فقال: فهذا تحريم لحوم الإبل والألبان إنما جاء من يعقوب وأنتم تقولون إنه من دين إبراهيم، والقصة في ذلك أن يعقوب عليه الصلاة والسلام نذر لله إن رزقه اللّٰه عشرة من الأولاد ودخل بيت المقدس سالما ليذبحن واحدا منهم تقربا إلى اللّٰه تبارك وتعالى فرزقه اللّٰه عشرة أولاد فلما كبروا ذهب إلى بيت المقدس حتى قرب من بيت المقدس رمية حجر فتلقاه ملك على صورة رجل فقال له يا يعقوب أنت قوي وأنا أحب مصارعتك، فتصارعا ولم يصرع أحد منهما الآخر، فغمزه الملك برجله في فخذه فأصابه مرض عرق النسا فدخل بيت المقدس وهو مريض مرض
عرق النسا، فتألم من هذا المرض وصار يصيح في الليل فنذر أنه إن برئ من هذا المرض يترك لحوم الإبل وألبانها. هذا هو سبب النذر فصار بنو إسرائيل تبعا ليعقوب في هذا[7] وأرادوا أن يجعلوه على دين إبراهيم فكذبَهم اللّٰه تبارك وتعالى بقوله «كُلُّ الطَّعَامِ كَانَ حِلَّا» حلالا (لِبَنِي إِسْرَآءِيلَ إِلاَّ مَا حَرَّمَ إِسْرَاءِيلٌ) الذي هو يعقوب (عَلَىٰ نَمْسِهِ،) وهو الإبل
(من قَبْلِ أن تُنَزَّلَ التَّوْرِيَةُ وهذا قبل نزول التوراة قُلْ فَاتُواْ بِالتَّوْرِيَةِ قَاتْلُوهَا) ليتبين صدق قولكم إِى كُنتُمْ صَدِقِين فبهتوا قَمَى إِمْتَرِى عَلَى اللَّهِ الْكَذِبَ مِنْ بَعْدِ ذَلِكَ) ظهور الحجة بأن التحريم إنما كان من جهة يعقوب لا على عهد إبراهيم (قَأُوْلَبِكَ هُمُ الظِّلِمُونُ قَلْ صَدَقَ ألَّهُ ى في هذا كجميع ما أخبر به (اتَّبِعُوأ مِلَّةَ إِنْرَهِيَ) التي أنا عليها ( حَيْبَاه فُلْ صَدَقَ اللَّهُ في هذا كجميع ما أخبر به (قَاتَّبِعُواْ مِلَّةَ إِبْرَهِيمَ التي أنا عليها حَنِيماكِ مائلا عن كل دين إلى الإسلام (وَمَا كَانَ مِنَ ألْمُشْرِ كِينَ) أخبر الله تبارك وتعالى أن هذا التحريم من قبل يعقوب عليه الصلاة والسلام وهذه عبادة الإنسان يمنع نفسه من شهو الحلال تقربا إلى اللّه تبارك وتعالى كما فعل إسرائيل، فكذلك كل الطعام كان حلا لعبد اللّه إذا سلك إلى حضرة اللّٰه تبارك وتعالى إلا ما حرم السالك على نفسه مجاهدة لنفسه من قبل أن تنزل التوراة قبل أن يأتي الفتح الأكبر «قَمَرِ إِجْتَرِى عَلَى أللَّهِ ٱلْكَذِبَ مِنْ بَعْدِ ذَلِكَ) بدعوى الوصول إلى اللّٰه تبارك وتعالى بدون السلوك «فَأَوْلَيِكَ هُمْ ألظَلِمُونَ» الذين وضعوا الأشياء في غير محلها. «فُلْ صَدَقَ اللَّةُ فَاتَّبِعُواْ مِلَّةَ إِبْرَٰهِيمَ حَنِيفاࣰۖ» الإنسان هو العالم الأكبر، اللّٰه تبارك وتعالى خلق الأشياء فجعلهم أقساما قسم نوراني وعيشهم ذكر اللّٰه وعبادة اللّٰه موافق لجنسهم هم نورانيون وقوهم من جنسهم نوراني أيضا، وقسم خلقهم اللّٰه جسمانين كالحيوانات عيشهم موافق لجنسهم جسماني وليس عندهم عبادة، والإنسان خلقه اللّه فجمع فيه بين الجسمانية والنورانية فهو عيشه جسماني موافق لجسمه الطعام والشراب وعيش روحه ذكر اللّٰه تبارك وتعالى لأنه روحاني فإذا جاهد الإنسان نفسه حتى طهرها من جميع الشهوات لحق بالروحانيين فصار من جنس الملك وهو خير منه، فيوجد من البشر من هو خير من الملائكة، وإذا اشتغل بشهوات نفسه حتى أمات روحانيته باتباع حيوانيته فيصير كأنه من جنس الحيوان "إِنْ هُمُدَ إِلاَّ كَالاَنْعَامِ بَلْ هُمُوَ أَضَلُّ"كما قال في الآية '" بَينهُمْ ظَالِمٌ لِنَفْسِهِ، وَمِنْهُم مُفْتَصِدٌ وَمِنْهُمْ سَابِقُ بِالْخَيْرَاتِ". فالظالم لنفسه من اتبع الشهوات حنى
أمات الروحانية بالحيوانية، ذلك هو الذي قال فيه "إِنْ هُمُ إِلَّ كَالاَنْعَمِ بَلْ هُمْوَ أَضَلُّ" وقال فيهم: "أَوْلِيِكَ هُمْ شَرُّ الْبَرِيَّةٍ". ومنهم مقتصد بأن اشتغل بالشهوات الحيوانية تارة وتارة بعبادة اللّٰه تبارك وتعالى "خَلَطَواْ عَمَلًا صَلِحاً وَاحَرَ سَيِّئِا عَسَى اللَّهُ أَنْ يَقُوبَ عَلَيْهِمْدَ".
وقسم سابق بالخيرات طهروا الروح من شهوات النفس حتى أماتوا النفس بالكلية ففنوا في اللّه وبقوا "أَوْلَيِكَ هُمْ خَيْرُ ألْبَرِيَّةٍ" والسالك بمجاهدته للنفس ومنعها عن شهواتِها تابع ملة إبراهيم. صدق اللّٰه فيما أخبر أن من أنفق جميع ما عنده نال مواصلة اللّٰه تبارك وتعالى، من كان الله كان اللّٰه له. فاتبعوا إذاً ملة إبراهيم الذي أسلم أمواله للضيفان وولده للقربان ونفسه للنيران "حَنِيماً وَمَا كَانَ مِنَ الْمُشْرِكِينَ" إبراهيم انفرد لله وحده وجعل كل ما سوى اللّٰه عدوا له " جَنَّهَمْ عَدُوُّلِىَ إِلاَّ رَبَّ الْعَلَمِينَ". بهذا الطريق يجد الإنسان مواصلة اللّٰه تبارك وتعالى
"وَالذِيسَ جَهَدُواْ بِينَا لَنَهْدِيَنَّهُمْ سُبُلَنَا وَإِنَّ أُللَّهَ لَمَعَ الْمُحْسِنِينَ". أما من ادعى الوصول إلى اللّٰه تبارك وتعالى بدون هذا الطريق فهو كاذب كما دلت عليه هذه الآية.
"وَمَا كَالَ مِنَ
الْمُشْرِكِينَ " كلما ذكر إبراهيم برأه من الشرك.
ونزل لما قالت اليهود: قبلتنا قبل قبلتكم يعنون بيت المقدس قال الله: (إِنَّ أَوَّلَ بَيْتِ وُضِعَ) متعّبدا {لِلنَّاس) في الأرض ( للذِى بِبَكَّةَ) هو البيت الذي بيكة \- بكة لغة في مكة \- أو بكة البقعة التي عليها الكعبة خصوصا[8]، أو مكة القرية وبكة هي ما تحت البيت وهذا
أولى لأن البيت كان قبل القرية، فإذاً ما عليه البيت هو بكة ومكة هي القرية وما حولها
"هو الذي كف أيديهم عنكم وأيديكم عنهم ببطن مكة"، سميت بكة لأنّها تبك أعناق الجبابرة[9]. هو أول بيت وضع متعبدا للناس بناه الملائكة قبل خلق آدم بألفى عام[10]، ووضع الأقصى قال جلال[11] وبينهما أربعون سنة وهذا سبق قلم منه، إنما الملائكة بنوا الكعبة في خلق آدم بألفي سنة، ولما خلق اللّٰه آدم صار يحج هذا البيت وبعد ذلك أمره اللّٰه بيه ثانيا فبناه آدم وبقي أربعين سنة يحج هذا البيت، وبعد أربعين سنة أمره اللّٰه ببناء بيت المقدس فكان بينهما أربعون سنة أي بين بناء آدم للكعبة وبنائه لبيت المقدس[12]، وأمار قال المفسر من أن الملائكة بنوه وبين بناء الملائكة وبناء القدس أربعون سنة فهذا سيق نهم منه، بل بينهما ألفان وأربعون سنة[13]. وفي الحديث (أول ما ظهر على وجه الماء عند خلق
السماوات والأرض زبدة بيضاء فدحيت الأرض من تحتها وهي هذه الكعبة)[14]. بيت اللّٰه في مقابلته البيت المعمور الذي في السماء (مُبَرَكاً) بيتا ذا بركة، بركته أمن الوحوش حوله وعدم تعرض من استجار به لأي سوء، إذا لقي إنسان قاتل أبيه عنده لا يتعرض له (وَهُدىً لِلْعَلَمِينَ) لأنه قبلتهم (فِيهِ ايَاتٌ بَيِّنَٰتْ) منها (مَفَامُ إِبْرَهِيمٌ) الحجر الذي قام عليه عند بناء البيت فأثر قدماه فيه وبقي إلى الآن مع تطاول الزمان وتداول الأيدي عليه، ومنها تضعيف الحسنات فيه، وأن الطير لا يعلو[15] (وَمَى دَخَلَهُو كَانَ ءَامِناَ من دخل مقام إبراهيم كان آمنا لا يُتعرض إليه بقتل أو ظلم وغير ذلك، هذا من بركة هذا البيت، ومن بركته كثرة الثواب لمن يحجه (من حج فلم يرفث ولم يفسق رجع من ذنوبه كيوم ولدته أمه)[16]. من حج مرة فقد أدى فرضه ومن حج ثانية فقد داين ربه ومن حج ثالثة فقد حرم شعره وجسده من النار[17]. وهذا البيت حجه جميع الأنبياء إلا أربعة منهم، من آدم إلى محمد صلى اللّٰه عليه وسلم ما فيهم نبي إلا وحج إلا أربعة منهم: هود وصالح ولوط وإدريس، ما سواهم من الأنبياء والمرسلين كلهم حجوا هذا البيت، لو كان بيتا عاديا فقط وتردد عليه الأنبياء والصالحون من أول الدهر إلى يومنا هذا لكفاه بركة لاسيما وهو بيت
الله تبارك وتعالى، بناه الملائكة فأتوا بالحجر الأسود أبيض من اللبن من ياقوت الجنة[18] وجعلوه في الركن، وقال الحق جل وعلا إنه يمين اللّٰه في أرضه من مسه فكأنما صافح الرب تبارك وتعالى[19]، ولما بناه آدم وبناه شئث ولده، بناه إبراهيم رابعة، عند بناء إبراهيم أوتي بهذا المقام وهو حجر قدر ثلاثة أذرع كان يقف عليه إبراهيم لبناء الكعبة، المهندس جبريل عليه الصلاة والسلام والباني إبراهيم خليل اللّه والتلميذ الذي يعينه إسماعيل وميكائيل هو الذي يساعد إسماعيل وكلما اشتغل إبراهيم بالبناء حتى طال البناء على الحجر الذي يقف عليه يتطاول الحجر المقام حتى يبلغ إبراهيم الكعبة، بناه على هذا الشكل الذي تجدون ثلاثون ذراعا والذي يقف عليه ثلاثة أذرع فقط، وأثر أقدام إبراهيم على المقام إلى الآن، آثار قدم إبراهيم موجودة كأنه وطئه الآن. كان الناس يتبركون به وغطاه السعوديون مخافة أن يراه الناس جهلا منهم وهذا المقام أيضا من ياقوت الجنة، لا تجد أمة في الدنيا عندهم شيء تُحقق أنه من الجنة إلا أمة محمد صلى اللّٰه عليه وسلم، مقام إبراهيم والحجر الأسود
من ياقوت الجنة[20] ليس في الدنيا شيء من الجنة إلا هذان. فلما بناه إبراهيم هذا البناء وأتم بناءه أمره اللّٰه أن ينادي الناس لحج هذا البيت، فقال كيف أناديهم وهم معدومون في أصلاب آبائهم؟ قال اللّٰه تبارك وتعالى: عليك الدعاء والإسماع علي أنا، فوقف على جبل أبي فبيس وقال: أيها الناس إن ربكم قد بنى بيتا ودعاكم إلى حجه فحجوا، استجاب الحجاج كلا من سائر أنحاء العالم وهم في العدم، من استجاب في ذلك اليوم لا بد أن يحج ومن لم يستجب لا يحج ولو توفرت عنده الأسباب، من استجاب مرة واحدة حج مرة، ومن استجاب مرتين حج مرتين، ومرارا كذلك[21]. فتجد الحاج إذا حج يحن إلى العودة إلى تلك الأماكن بدعوة إبراهيم
"فاجْعَلَ آفئدَةَ مِنَ النَّاسِ تَهْوِي إِلَيْهِمْ". تردد واحد من الصالحين
للحج حتى حج ستين مرة فجلس يوما وهو يفكر في حجاته هل تقبلت منه أم لا فسمع صوتا يقول: يا فلان هل تدعو إلى بيتك إلا من تحب؟ فقوي رجاؤه أن اللّٰه استجاب له[22].
